clue.text: Paddy gets so much foreign spirit

parts.note: tant is French for so much, hence foreign
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: An Irishman is handed a generous measure of some imported liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman, but here it is the British informal word for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a fit of bad temper, an outburst of rage.

clue.text: It's conceited for the owner to play it

definitions.text: It's conceited for the owner to play it

parts.words: It's conceited for the owner to play it
parts.note: the idiom about boasting is to blow your own brass instrument

explanation.surface: Showing off by performing on one's own instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow one's own horn of this kind is the idiom for boasting about oneself.

clue.text: Capital rising in endless social upheaval

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word in is read upwards, backwards
upheaval means the letters are thrown about and rearranged
endless means the last letter of social is dropped

explanation.surface: A city in revolt amid constant social unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses IN to NI; 'endless' cuts SOCIAL to SOCIA, which 'upheaval' rearranges into COSIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, divided between Greek and Turkish communities.

clue.text: Movement in which boy takes first note

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name
do (doh) is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A piece of music in which a young lad plays the opening note.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form often used for the final movement of a sonata or concerto.

clue.text: Material for idle talk in artificially homely surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the rearranged letters go around the word for idle talk
artificially means the letters are rearranged in an unnatural order

parts.note: gas is informal for idle chatter

explanation.surface: Fabric for gossip in a fake cosy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificially' makes MOYHEL, which 'surroundings' wraps around the gossip; 'in' is a link. Moygashel is a village in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Moygashel is an Irish linen dress fabric, named after a village in County Tyrone.

clue.text: No right for damned one still awaiting verdict

indicators.note: no right means the letter for right is dropped from the word

parts.note: damned means accursed

explanation.surface: A condemned soul is denied justice before the court has decided.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant on trial, not yet found guilty or innocent, is the person charged in court.

clue.text: To make gentle progress it's better avoiding extremes

indicators.note: avoiding extremes means the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: Taking it slowly is wiser than going to extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like an adjective but is someone who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow leisurely pace, making unhurried progress.

clue.text: Molest while in charge — it could carry a charge

indicators.note: in means the word for molest goes inside the word for charge

parts.note: care means charge, as in a child in your care
to touch can mean to interfere with or molest

explanation.surface: An official abusing someone placed under their protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is a cartridge case or an ornate shield-shaped frame, which in heraldry bears a charge.

clue.text: Arrangement of Israeli composer

indicators.note: an arrangement re-orders the letters, as a musical arrangement re-orders notes

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement by a Jewish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Salieri was an Italian composer at the Viennese court, rival of Mozart.

clue.text: Old poet captured the old leading lady

indicators.note: captured means the archaic article is held inside the poet's name

parts.note: John Donne was a seventeenth-century poet
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A Jacobean poet seized the elderly star actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most senior or respected woman in a field, its leading lady.

clue.text: Weird taste of real ale?

definitions.meaning: real ale is served from the cask, never from a tin, so its flavour is not of the can

explanation.surface: An odd flavour in the traditional beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird is strangely, eerily out of the ordinary; the second reading splits the word as not tinned.

clue.text: Novelist left in Lancashire town

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the novelist's name

parts.note: Fanny Burney was an eighteenth-century English novelist

explanation.surface: A writer abandoned in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny Burney wrote Evelina; Lancashire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnley is a mill town in Lancashire, north-west England, home of a well-known football club.

clue.text: Ministerial office, beyond having to speak

parts.note: past means beyond, as in past the church
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: A minister who has moved on still has to give speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of a pastor, a Christian minister, is his or her charge or ministry.

clue.text: Lines on the cinema

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Poetry read aloud at the picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Odeon is a British chain of picture houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a well-known British chain of picture houses, and the name came to mean a cinema.

clue.text: Wear down with front teeth (back, in a manner of speaking)

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: to gnaw is to wear down by biting

indicators.note: front of teeth means its first letter

explanation.surface: Biting away at something with the incisors, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GNAW plus T (front of teeth) into the answer. 'front teeth' wants to be incisors; it is the first letter of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of voice, a distinctive accent or way of speaking.

clue.text: Vigorous contortion of MacStingy

indicators.note: a contortion twists the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A stingy Scotsman's energetic twisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastic means athletic, involving vigorous physical exercise and agility.

clue.text: With Howard's leader-ship chaotic Tory epic describes many a politician

indicators.note: the leader of Howard's is its first letter
chaotic means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe at the disordered saga of Michael Howard's time leading the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Howard led the Conservative (Tory) Party; 'leader-ship' gives his initial H, which 'chaotic' shuffles with TORY EPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic's view: a politician often professes virtues he lacks, the mark of a two-faced pretender.

clue.text: Belief in diverse divinities — one such is among them

parts.note: Pan, the Greek god of the wild, is one such divinity

indicators.note: among means the word is goes inside the word them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polytheism, where one particular god lives among the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is the doctrine that God is everything, also used for tolerance or worship of all gods.

clue.text: Wallaby in 21 with no jump over a bit of sea

indicators.note: the answer to 21 is retreat, and something in retreat goes backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a jump over the sea puts the leap around it

parts.note: leap means jump
the Med, the Mediterranean, is a sea, part of the seas generally

explanation.surface: A marsupial in hiding that cannot hop across a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference itself is the reversal signal: 21-down's answer means withdrawal, so 'in 21' reads the run backwards. 'over' puts the jump around the sea, giving LEMEDAP before reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The pademelon is a small Australian and New Guinean marsupial, one of the smallest kinds of wallaby.

clue.text: Approval for archbishop when in a hole

indicators.note: in means the archbishop goes inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: Cheers for a church leader stuck in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or applause, showing approval.

clue.text: Slaver starts down the river

indicators.note: starts of down means its first letter

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in Lancashire and Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A slave trader sets off downstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaver' looks like a slave trader but is the verb to drool; the Ribble is a river in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, to drool.

clue.text: Composer in anger starts to look back

indicators.note: look back means the whole assembled piece is read in reverse order
in means the first letter of look goes inside the word for anger

parts.note: anger means rage

indicators.note: starts to look means its first letter

explanation.surface: A musician turns round in fury to glance behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside RAGE to give RAGLE, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Force to become less well nourished, like Ruth

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force
leaner means thinner, less well fed

explanation.surface: Compelling someone to slim down, as happened to a biblical woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Old Testament, Ruth gleaned leftover grain in the fields of Boaz.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth gathered left-behind grain at harvest, so she is the biblical example of such a gatherer.

clue.text: Withdraw on account of a celebration

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a treat is a special celebration or outing

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a party on financial grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw, to pull back from a position.

clue.text: A girl depicted in porcelain

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman portrayed on a china figurine.
explanation.definitionFit: Arita is a Japanese porcelain, named after the town in Kyushu where it is made.

clue.text: Echoing voice entertained the old king

indicators.note: entertained means the word the is held inside
an echo comes back, so the voice is read in reverse order

parts.note: treble is a singing voice, the highest boy's part
taken as written

explanation.surface: A resounding voice performed for the ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echoing' turns the voice round to ELBERT, and 'entertained' sits the article inside after its first letter. Ethelbert ruled Kent around 600 AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelbert was an Anglo-Saxon king of Kent, the first English monarch converted to Christianity.

clue.text: Equip to put a stop to rejection of Brussels

parts.note: an end is a stop, a finish

indicators.note: rejection turns the letters back, reading them in reverse

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: Fitting out for halting a rebuff from the European bureaucrats.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or provide someone with a quality, to equip them.

clue.text: Language involved in formulating a dodgy dossier

indicators.note: involved in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Words used in cooking up a dubious government document.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dodgy dossier' was the 2003 UK government report on Iraq's weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the language of ancient Rome, still used in law and science.

clue.text: Article owing to editor, it might be argued

parts.note: owing is in debt, so the article, a, placed in debt makes these letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper item handed to its editor might prove controversial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'owing' is read as 'in debt', so 'Article owing' is A in DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something debated has been argued over, discussed formally from opposing sides.

clue.text: Concentrated on how numbers are recorded on earth

parts.note: in the decimal system numbers are recorded in tens

explanation.surface: Wondering how figures are kept down here.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means concentrated, strong or extreme in degree, like an intense flavour.

clue.text: It's well drawn in Wonderland

parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of sisters who lived at the bottom of a well and drew a sticky syrup from it

explanation.surface: Praise for the illustrations of Alice's adventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' looks like illustrated, as in Tenniel's pictures; in the Mad Tea Party the syrup is drawn from a well like water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dormouse's tale at the Mad Tea Party features a well full of this syrup, from which the sisters drew it.

clue.text: A term in construction of religious edifice

indicators.note: construction means the letters are built up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An architectural word used in building a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is given.
